vocabulary.meaning: a telephone connected by a fixed physical line rather than a mobile network
examples: Many young households no longer have a landline.
My grandparents still use their landline every day.

vocabulary.meaning: the part of a telephone that is held to speak and listen
examples: She picked up the handset when the phone rang.
Old handsets were connected to the phone by a cable.

vocabulary.meaning: a telephone connection installed at a permanent location
examples: Businesses once depended heavily on fixed-line phones.
Fixed-line use has declined as mobile phones have spread.

vocabulary.meaning: a portable telephone that connects through a wireless network
examples: Mobile phones have replaced landlines for many people.
I rarely make calls from anything except my mobile phone.

vocabulary.meaning: to enter a telephone number in order to make a call
examples: Dial the number and wait for someone to answer.
Older phones had a wheel that people used to dial numbers.

vocabulary.meaning: high-speed internet access, often delivered through fixed communications infrastructure
examples: Some households keep a fixed line mainly for broadband.
Faster broadband changed home communication.

vocabulary.meaning: no longer useful because something newer has replaced it
examples: Some people think landlines are becoming obsolete.
The device became obsolete within a decade.

vocabulary.meaning: all the people living together in one home
examples: The survey asked whether each household had a landline.
Mobile-only households are increasingly common.

vocabulary.meaning: the system that connects telephones and carries calls
examples: The traditional telephone network is being modernised.
Old telephone networks require expensive maintenance.

vocabulary.meaning: the exchange of information between people
examples: Mobile technology has transformed personal communication.
Landlines were once central to household communication.
